merger_description:
Zoetis Holdings LLC (**Zoetis**), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Zoetis Inc., proposes to acquire the global animal genomic testing business (**Neogen Genomics**) of Neogen Corporation (the **Acquisition**).

Animal genomic testing involves the analysis of an animal’s DNA from samples like hair or tissue and integrating this genetic information with performance and pedigree data primarily maintained by breed societies and industry associations. This process increases the accuracy in prediction of the animal’s genetic merit, helping breeders (e.g. farmers) make early, informed decisions in relation to traits like health, fertility, production (milk/meat) and feed efficiency, as well as physical characteristics.

Both Zoetis and Neogen Corporation are US-listed companies that supply genomic testing services in respect of livestock globally, including in Australia.

Zoetis supplies genomic testing services from its laboratory located in Kalamazoo, Michigan in the US, and Neogen Genomics supplies services from its laboratory located in Brisbane.

The Acquisition will involve Zoetis acquiring all of the shares in the companies within the Neogen Corporation group that supply genomic testing services globally, as well as certain non-Australian assets of Neogen Genomics.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Relevant areas of competition
items: Whether other herd improvement methods or services are substitutes for genomic testing for cattle in Australia, including whether other herd improvement services are as efficient and effective as genomic testing, the level of take-up of genomic testing and in what circumstances breed societies require genomic testing to be used.
The extent of the regulatory requirements for switching or expanding into supplying genomic testing for cattle that are faced by suppliers of genomic testing for other livestock.
The extent to which there are discrete product markets for dairy cattle and beef cattle.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Competition effects in the supply of genomic testing services for cattle in Australia
items: The extent to which remaining alternative suppliers of genomic testing services for cattle in Australia would meaningfully constrain the merged entity.
The likelihood of timely new entry and expansion to constrain the merged entity in the supply of genomic testing services for cattle in Australia.

The extent to which cattle breed associations could credibly threaten to bypass the merged entity, either by self-supplying genomic testing services for cattle in Australia and/or sponsoring new entry or expansion.

The extent to which the merged entity would gain access to additional genetic information, whether this information would provide the merged entity with competitive advantages not available to its rivals and the effect of any such advantages on competition.
